_note: The reviewer's scored rubric (hub-qc skill). Every criterion is pass or fail with one line of evidence, recorded in spec.review.rubric. Any fail sends the page back to rework with a field-level fix. The writer runs the same rubric on itself before QC. Criteria come from real rejections (rules/CONTENT_DEFECTS.md); add one only with Divit's sign-off.

criteria.test: The H1, meta title and hero state the primary's whole job, not one feature of it and not a sibling page's topic.
The page delivers what the top 10 and PAA show searchers want (software comparison, examples, templates, how-to), at that depth.
Every section speaks to this page's buyer in their vocabulary; no hub-level boilerplate; the Emergent table column uses this category's variant.
Every paragraph opens with a full sentence that says what happens; no keyword labels or fragments.
Sentences end on the important word, vary in length, carry one idea each; no tacked-on clauses, no run-on lists.
Every paragraph would ship unedited on Stripe's or Linear's site; nothing reads machine-written.
Every claim is approved, every competitor fact comes from the library, every number agrees with every other.
It reads as its own page, not a sibling with the nouns swapped.
15 real questions, each answered in its first sentence; links help the reader; secondaries read naturally.
Each tab shows one moment that matches its copy word for word on names, numbers and outcomes; panels read full; nothing collides or crowds.
